key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over weeks to months, often noticed by patient or family member. LOCATION: ANYWHERE on body - sun-exposed areas (face, arms, legs) most common. DURATION: Progressive over weeks to months, may change rapidly. CHARACTER: VARIABLE - may be raised, flat, pigmented, or non-pigmented. AGGRAVATING: SUN exposure, trauma, irritation. RELIEVING: AVOIDING sun exposure, protective clothing. TIMING: Progressive over weeks to months, may change rapidly. SEVERITY: 1-3/10 pain, usually asymptomatic. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Usually ASYMPTOMATIC, may have mild itching, may have bleeding or ulceration, may have color changes. KEY POSITIVES: Asymmetry, irregular borders, color variation, diameter >6mm, evolution over time (ABCDE criteria). KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no systemic symptoms, no rapid growth (unless aggressive).

excludes.patient_friendly: all at once or very quickly

red_flags: Rapid growth or change in appearance - possible aggressive cancer, needs urgent evaluation
Bleeding or ulceration - possible advanced cancer, needs urgent evaluation
Multiple lesions or family history of skin cancer - high risk, needs urgent evaluation
Lesion with satellite nodules - possible metastasis, needs urgent evaluation
Lesion with regional lymphadenopathy - possible metastasis, needs urgent evaluation
